board_entry: VERIFY (MECH-SEED's strongest surviving objection) / B-ROUTE (key side)
question: MECH-SEED seed-varied the MATCHED-k keys-vs-control comparison only (k=12, k=16), while DIAG-CONTROLCURVE relocated the frozen control's true MT minimum to k=10 -- which shrinks the OWN-OPTIMUM dMT from ~-0.21 to -0.1363 on one seed. Does the fair, own-optimum key-side claim survive seed variation above DIAG-NOISE's measured paired resolution of +-0.0494 MT, and is the control's MT argmin itself seed-stable at k=10?
variable_under_test: AM_SEED_OFFSET in {0,1000,2000} (which 32 of each document's ~500 reference conversations the closed-form solve is fitted to), crossed with k = number of documents written. NOTHING WAS RE-TRAINED: all 40 evals read pre-existing per-document `cache-after-doc-*.pt` snapshots produced by MECH-SEED (offsets 1000/2000) and by MECH-KEYS/DIAG-KEYCURVE (offset 0).

numbers._note: qa/mt are the number this task was dispatched to produce: the frozen-key CONTROL at k=10 (DIAG-CONTROLCURVE's argmin), averaged over the three seed offsets -- MT 2.4083292484283447 / 2.491347312927246 / 2.472822427749634 and QA 1.9674913883209229 / 2.0084433555603027 / 1.9783906936645508. The keys arm's k=12 seed-mean is unchanged from MECH-SEED (MT 2.2680621147155762 / QA 1.9467895825703938). solve_s / phase2_e2e_s / gradient_steps are 0 because nothing was trained: this job is 40 evals on checkpoints that already existed.

diagnostics.headline: THE OWN-OPTIMUM KEY-SIDE CLAIM SURVIVES SEED VARIATION. Keys at k=12 vs control at k=10 gives dMT -0.1363 / -0.2218 / -0.2102 at offsets 0/1000/2000 (mean -0.1894, range 0.0855) -- all three 2.8-4.5x DIAG-NOISE's measured paired resolution of 0.0494, and all three also clear the conservative composite 0.1055. Letting the control take ITS OWN per-seed MT argmin (k=10/12/6) instead of a pinned k=10 weakens but does not break it: dMT -0.1363 / -0.1791 / -0.1481, mean -0.1545, still 2.8-3.6x the yardstick. The adversarial pairing -- the keys arm's WORST seed at k=12 against the control's BEST (seed, k) pair anywhere on its 16-point curve -- is -0.1363, still 2.76x the yardstick.
diagnostics.second_headline: BUT THE CONTROL'S MT ARGMIN IS NOT SEED-STABLE. It moves k=10 (offset 0) -> k=12 (offset 1000) -> k=6 (offset 2000). The movement is itself inside noise -- at every offset the gap from the best k to the runner-up is 0.0060-0.0233, i.e. 2-8x SMALLER than the 0.0494 paired resolution -- so the control's argmin is being selected out of noise and 'k=10 is the control's optimum' is a one-seed statement. What IS stable is the VALUE of the control's minimum: 2.4083 / 2.4486 / 2.4107, range 0.0403, below the resolution. That is why the comparison survives even though the argmin wanders.

correctness_gates.note: all six reproduce to all 16 printed digits. The keys offset-0 gate is stronger than a numeric match: the checkpoint evaluated (MECH-SEED run A2, cache-after-doc-009) is sha256-IDENTICAL (ba592c96c44b4828...) to DIAG-KEYCURVE's own keys run snapshot, so this is the same bytes through the same harness in a new session.

diagnostics.no_snapshot_was_missing: all 16 cache-after-doc-*.pt exist in all six run directories used; k=10 == cache-after-doc-009-f77cecfb.pt in every case; nothing was substituted and nothing had to be re-run.

own_optimum_comparison_as_dispatched.definition: keys at its argmin k=12 vs control at DIAG-CONTROLCURVE's argmin k=10, per offset.

QA.verdict: the QA half of the own-optimum claim remains UNCONFIRMED -- only offset 1000 clears, and the seed-mean -0.038 is below the yardstick.

own_optimum_comparison_each_arm_at_its_O.definition: the strictest fair version: for each offset, the control takes the minimum of ITS OWN 16-point MT curve at that offset (k=10/12/6), and the keys arm takes the minimum over the k measured at that offset ({1..16} at offset 0; {10,12,16} at 1000/2000, argmin k=12 in all three).
own_optimum_comparison_each_arm_at_its_O.caveat: the keys arm's curve is only 3 points deep at the non-zero offsets, so its per-seed minimum could be LOWER than 2.2695/2.2626 -- that direction would only enlarge |dMT|. The control's curve is fully mapped (16/16 k) at every offset, so its minimum cannot be lower than reported. The estimate is therefore conservative against the keys arm.

adversarial_pairing.note: keys' WORST seed at its argmin k=12 (2.2720184326171875, offset 0) against the control's BEST value anywhere on its curve at any seed (2.4083292484283447, offset 0, k=10).
adversarial_pairing.verdict: the MT effect survives the least favourable pairing the data allows; the QA effect does not, at any pairing.

common_k_comparison_at_k10.definition: both arms read at k=10 (the control's offset-0 argmin), the 'both arms at a common k' version the brief asked for.
common_k_comparison_at_k10.note: at a common k=10 the MT effect is present at every seed (-0.089 / -0.218 / -0.169) but the offset-0 value -0.0887 does NOT clear the conservative composite 0.1055. QA flips sign across seeds and is unresolvable.

argmin_stability_control_MT.provenance_of_each_curve: offset 0 = DIAG-CONTROLCURVE (all 16 k), re-gated here at k=10; offsets 1000/2000 = measured by THIS job (k=1..11,13,14,15 MT) plus MECH-SEED's k=12 and k=16 (k=12 re-run here as the correctness gate and reproduced exactly). All 16 k are populated at every offset.
argmin_stability_control_MT.plain_statement: the control's MT argmin is NOT seed-stable: k=10, 12, 6 at the three offsets. Every one of those minima is separated from its own runner-up by less than half the measured paired resolution, so the argmin location is not resolvable at this eval size -- the 'own-optimum' comparison is therefore itself seed-dependent, and that must be said. What is resolvable is that the control's best achievable MT sits at 2.41-2.45 at every seed while the keys arm sits at 2.26-2.27.

matched_k_reference_unchanged.note: reproduced from MECH-SEED for context; this job re-ran the control k=12 MT at both non-zero offsets as its gate and got bit-identical values.

diagnostics.mass_on_S: NOT APPLICABLE / NOT NEWLY MEASURED: this job performed no AM solve (40 evals, 0 gradient steps, 0 solves), so there is no new write to report mass for. The relevant existing figures are MECH-SEED's solve-time ref_mass_on_S -- keys 0.3136 / 0.3615 / 0.3587 vs control 0.1452 / 0.1460 -- and DIAG-KEYCURVE's eval-time mass_on_S at k=10 (keys 0.2212).

noise_discipline.explicit: the correct yardstick for these comparisons is DIAG-NOISE's measured PAIRED resolution of +-0.0494 MT, not the inherited +-0.15 rule of thumb, which is ~3x too wide for paired same-example comparisons. Ranges over three seed offsets are RANGES OF THREE, not confidence intervals.

observations: 1) THE OWN-OPTIMUM CLAIM SURVIVES SEED VARIATION. Keys at its argmin k=12 against the control at DIAG-CONTROLCURVE's argmin k=10 gives dMT -0.13631 (offset 0), -0.22181 (offset 1000), -0.21019 (offset 2000): mean -0.18944, range 0.08550, same sign at every seed, every one of the three between 2.76x and 4.49x DIAG-NOISE's measured paired resolution of 0.0494, and every one also clearing the conservative composite 0.1055. The one-seed -0.1363 the board records is in fact the WEAKEST of the three seeds. 2) THE FOUR DISPATCHED EVALS: control at k=10 is MT 2.491347312927246 / QA 2.0084433555603027 at offset 1000 and MT 2.472822427749634 / QA 1.9783906936645508 at offset 2000. No snapshot was missing -- all 16 cache-after-doc-*.pt exist in all six run directories, k=10 is cache-after-doc-009-f77cecfb.pt in every one, and nothing had to be re-run or substituted. 3) ALL SIX CORRECTNESS GATES PASSED TO 16 DIGITS: control k=12 MT reproduced MECH-SEED exactly at both non-zero offsets (2.448606491088867 and 2.5163300037384033); control offset-0 k=10 reproduced DIAG-CONTROLCURVE exactly (MT 2.4083292484283447 / QA 1.9674913883209229); keys offset-0 k=10 reproduced DIAG-KEYCURVE exactly (MT 2.319589376449585 / QA 1.968939185142517) from a checkpoint that is sha256-identical to the one DIAG-KEYCURVE evaluated. 4) THE ADVERSARIAL PAIRING STILL CLEARS. The keys arm's worst seed at k=12 (2.2720184326171875) against the control's best value anywhere on its curve at any seed (2.4083292484283447) is dMT -0.13631, 2.76x the paired resolution and 1.29x the composite. 5) BUT THE CONTROL'S MT ARGMIN IS NOT SEED-STABLE, AND I AM REPORTING THAT PLAINLY. Mapping all 16 k of the control's MT curve at both non-zero offsets (13 new points per offset, plus MECH-SEED's k=12/16) puts the argmin at k=10 (offset 0), k=12 (offset 1000) and k=6 (offset 2000). So 'the control's optimum is k=10' is a one-seed fact, and the own-optimum comparison is itself seed-dependent. Two things blunt this: (a) at every offset the best k beats its own runner-up by only 0.0060-0.0233, i.e. 2-8x SMALLER than the 0.0494 resolution, so the argmin is being selected out of noise rather than located; and (b) the VALUE of the control's minimum is stable -- 2.4083 / 2.4486 / 2.4107, range 0.0403, itself below the resolution. 6) LETTING EACH ARM TAKE ITS OWN PER-SEED ARGMIN -- the strictest fair form -- gives dMT -0.13631 / -0.17907 / -0.14807, mean -0.15448, range 0.04276, all still 2.76-3.62x the paired resolution and all still clearing the composite 0.1055. This is the number that should be quoted for the fair comparison; it is conservative against the keys arm, whose curve is only three points deep at the non-zero offsets (its true per-seed minimum can only be lower). 7) AT A COMMON k=10 the keys arm is better at every seed -- dMT -0.08874 / -0.21790 / -0.16887, mean -0.15850 -- but the offset-0 value does not clear the composite 0.1055, so the common-k version is the weakest of the three framings. 8) THE QA HALF REMAINS UNCONFIRMED, as the board already says. At the own optima dQA is -0.01148 / -0.06872 / -0.03375 (mean -0.038): only offset 1000 clears the 0.0539 QA paired resolution. At a common k=10 the sign flips (+0.00145 at offset 0). Adversarially paired it is -0.01148. 9) PROVENANCE: 40 evals, 40 wandb URLs, 40/40 verified by fixed-string grep to have loaded the checkpoint they were given, all killed after their `Eval loss` line per RUNBOOK §1, all logging the resolved package path /tmp/amsnap_verifyoptima/cartridges. The pin earned its keep: repo HEAD moved cb0b6b4 -> 90f1d54 mid-job and the working tree acquired live uncommitted edits to cartridges/am/{__init__,continual,finetune,ranking}.py from a concurrent worker, while the snapshot manifest hash b71eaf15... was identical at launch, between the two runs and after. Nothing was trained (0 solves, 0 gradient steps); one GH200 held via flock; no source file was edited and nothing was committed. 10) CAVEATS I AM NOT ARGUING AWAY: three offsets are three samples of a coarse instrument (MT n=69) and the ranges quoted are ranges of three, not confidence intervals; the keys arm's per-seed curve is unmapped except at k in {10,12,16} for the non-zero offsets; the control's k=12 and k=16 points at the non-zero offsets are MECH-SEED's (k=12 MT re-run here and exact, k=16 reused); and the seed knob perturbs only which 32 reference conversations each document contributes, which is one of several stochastic choices, so it remains a lower bound on total run-to-run variance.
